doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What aggravates him on the bandstand
summary: Gates names bad sound and poor time as the worst things on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Just to wrap up, is there anything that really aggravates you on the bandstand?

Tight shoes. Not being able to hear myself is a big deal. Because as a singer we have no buttons to get that B flat out. If I can’t hear me, if I can’t hear the band and hear me in reference to the music that’s being played, it’s so hard to sing if you can’t hear yourself. Bad sound is probably the worst. And then after that is time. If we’re not in time then it’s not happening. I’d rather hear people — I mean I don’t want to hear anybody be out of tune, but I’d rather hear a little out of tune than a little out of time.
